items.followUp: Define a logic gate and name the two possible Boolean values.

rubric.why: Identifies Boolean algebra as a system involving logic or Boolean variables.
rubric.description: Identifies Boolean algebra as a system of logic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a mathematical or logical system.

rubric.why: States the two values used in Boolean algebra.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating 0 and 1, or true and false.

modelAnswer: Boolean algebra is a mathematical system used to represent and work with logical values and operations.
Its variables have only two possible values: 0 and 1 (false and true).

items.followUp: What are the two truth values used in Boolean logic?

rubric.why: Identifies one of the two truth values.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving true or 1.
Award 1 mark for giving false or 0.

modelAnswer: Truth values are the two values used to represent the result of a logical expression.

items.followUp: Why should personal information be protected online?

rubric.why: Identifies the information that data privacy concerns.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming personal information as the subject of privacy.

rubric.why: Explains that privacy involves protecting data from unauthorized access, use, or disclosure.
rubric.description: States what personal data is protected against.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning protection from unauthorized access, use, or disclosure.

modelAnswer: Data privacy is the protection of personal data and information.
It prevents that information from being accessed, used, or disclosed without permission.

items.followUp: What is a software product key used for?

rubric.why: Identifies the software key as a code or number associated with the software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming it as a product key, serial number, or activation code.

rubric.why: States the key's purpose in installing or activating software.
rubric.description: Explains what the key is used for.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is used to install or activate the software.

modelAnswer: A software key is a product code or serial number supplied with software.
It is used to install or activate the software; using an unauthorized key is a form of software piracy.

items.followUp: What is the role of a receiver in data communication?

rubric.why: Identifies the sender as the origin of the communication.
rubric.description: Identifies who or what the sender is.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the sender is a person or device that originates the data.

rubric.why: States that the sender sends data or a message to the receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the sender transmits data or a message.

modelAnswer: The sender is the person or device that originates a data communication.
It sends the data or message through a communication channel to the receiver.

items.followUp: What is one common way to share files over a network?

rubric.why: Identifies files as the items being shared.
rubric.description: Mentions files as the shared items.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that file sharing involves files.

rubric.why: Explains that files are made available to other users through a network or the Internet.
rubric.description: Explains how or with whom files are shared.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning sharing with other users over a network or the Internet.

modelAnswer: File sharing is the process of making files available to other users.
It is commonly done through a network or the Internet.

items.followUp: Name one wired and one wireless transmission medium.

rubric.why: Identifies a transmission medium as a path or channel.
rubric.description: Defines the medium as a path or channel.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as the path or channel used for transmission.

rubric.why: Identifies the communication endpoints connected by the medium.
rubric.description: States where the data travels between.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it carries data between a sender and receiver.

modelAnswer: A transmission medium is the path or channel through which data travels.
It carries data from a sender to a receiver, using a wired or wireless connection.

items.followUp: What is HTTPS, and how does it relate to HTTP?

rubric.why: Identifies HTTP as a protocol for web communication.
rubric.description: Identifies HTTP as a web communication protocol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming HTTP as a protocol used for web communication.

rubric.why: Describes the web communication or resources transferred using HTTP.
rubric.description: States what communicates or is transferred using HTTP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning transfer of web pages or resources between a browser/client and a web server.

modelAnswer: HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol and is a protocol used for communication on the World Wide Web.
It transfers web pages and other resources between a web browser (client) and a web server.
